SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #12
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why are cardinal points better than left and right for giving directions? (1 mark)
   A. They are shorter to say
   B. They do not change when you turn around
   C. They only work at night
   D. They are used only by pilots

2. Which of these people is most likely to use a compass? (1 mark)
   A. A cook
   B. A sailor
   C. A tailor
   D. A baby

3. What does a map key explain? (1 mark)
   A. The name of the map maker
   B. The weather
   C. The date of the map
   D. The meaning of the colours and symbols

4. What do we call the smaller parts into which a sub-county is divided? (1 mark)
   A. Plateaus
   B. Oceans
   C. Continents
   D. Wards

5. What is a valley? (1 mark)
   A. A very high peak
   B. A big lake
   C. A huge flat plain
   D. Low land between hills or mountains

6. Why does Kenya not have summer and winter like countries far from the equator? (1 mark)
   A. Kenya is too small
   B. Kenya lies on the equator so temperatures change little
   C. Kenya has no sun
   D. Kenya has no rain

7. What does interdependence mean? (1 mark)
   A. People fighting
   B. People doing everything themselves
   C. People living alone
   D. People needing and helping each other

8. Which place is used mainly for prayers and worship? (1 mark)
   A. Factory
   B. Market
   C. Church, mosque or temple
   D. Hospital

9. On a dot map where one dot means 1,000 people, an area has 7 dots. How many people live there? (1 mark)
   A. 70,000
   B. 7,000
   C. 700
   D. 70

10. Which pattern describes houses standing close together around a trading centre? (1 mark)
   A. Linear
   B. Clustered
   C. Scattered
   D. Empty

11. Why do some herding communities use portable dome-shaped houses? (1 mark)
   A. They are very tall
   B. They can be moved when the family moves
   C. They cannot be moved
   D. They are made of concrete

12. What is a kiondo? (1 mark)
   A. A drum
   B. A basket
   C. A shirt
   D. A house

13. Which of these is a school value? (1 mark)
   A. Stealing
   B. Bullying
   C. Honesty
   D. Cheating

14. When giving peer feedback, what should you do? (1 mark)
   A. Say nothing
   B. Laugh
   C. Say only bad things
   D. Say something you like and something to improve, politely

15. Which is NOT allowed in Kenyan schools? (1 mark)
   A. Talking to pupils
   B. Praising pupils
   C. Guiding and counselling pupils
   D. Beating pupils

16. Which national park in Narok County is famous for wildlife? (1 mark)
   A. Maasai Mara
   B. Kakamega
   C. Lake Victoria
   D. Nakuru town

17. Which county is famous for its tea farms? (1 mark)
   A. Kericho
   B. Turkana
   C. Lamu
   D. Marsabit

18. What is mining? (1 mark)
   A. Taking minerals from the ground
   B. Cutting hair
   C. Catching fish
   D. Growing maize

19. What is one way factories can protect the environment? (1 mark)
   A. Throw waste into rivers
   B. Burn tyres
   C. Treat waste before releasing it
   D. Cut all trees

20. Which factor makes a place suitable for a factory? (1 mark)
   A. Good roads and nearby workers
   B. No roads
   C. No water
   D. No workers

21. What is a cost? (1 mark)
   A. Profit
   B. Money received
   C. Salary
   D. Money spent on the project

22. Who keeps the money and records it in a school project? (1 mark)
   A. The treasurer
   B. The gatekeeper
   C. The safety officer
   D. The visitor

23. What should you do if something online makes you feel scared? (1 mark)
   A. Tell a trusted adult
   B. Reply angrily
   C. Meet the stranger
   D. Keep it secret

24. Which of these is a good digital citizen habit? (1 mark)
   A. Sending mean messages
   B. Asking an adult before going online
   C. Talking to strangers
   D. Sharing passwords

25. What is a peace corner? (1 mark)
   A. A shop
   B. A quiet place to calm down or talk through a problem
   C. A place to fight
   D. A place to hide

26. Which is an effect of child abuse? (1 mark)
   A. Higher marks
   B. More friends
   C. Fear and lost education
   D. Better health

27. A candidate gives sweets for votes. What is this? (1 mark)
   A. Democracy
   B. Fair campaigning
   C. Cheating
   D. Kindness

28. Who usually guides a Children's Government? (1 mark)
   A. A stranger
   B. A driver
   C. A teacher patron
   D. A police officer

29. Where does a county government get money? (1 mark)
   A. Only from gifts
   B. Only from fines
   C. From nowhere
   D. From the national government and local fees and taxes

30. Who is the head of a county government? (1 mark)
   A. The MCA
   B. The Governor
   C. The chief
   D. The Speaker

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Explain the meaning of profit and show how to find it. (3 marks)

32. The sugar factory employs 700 workers and the tea factory employs 400 workers. How many workers are there in the two factories together? Show your working. (3 marks)

33. Give three ways of conserving natural resources. (3 marks)

34. What is a school motto? (2 marks)

35. Explain how a farmer and a trader depend on each other. (3 marks)

36. Explain the difference between a physical feature and a built feature. Give one example of each. (4 marks)

37. County A covers 15 grid squares and County B covers 9 grid squares. Which is larger and by how many squares? Show your working. (3 marks)

38. Explain the difference between a ceremony and a festival and give one example of each. (4 marks)

39. List four rules that visitors should follow at a historic place. (4 marks)

40. Describe how a losing candidate should behave and why. (3 marks)

41. Name two places where you can find information about your school's history. (2 marks)

42. Give three ways in which the rainy season helps people. (3 marks)

43. Explain two ways of showing appreciation to people who help us. (2 marks)

44. Name the six aspects of traditional culture. (3 marks)

45. Describe how you would design a safety bib for pupils who walk to school. (4 marks)

46. State two things that a visitor can learn in a museum. (2 marks)

47. Name two artefacts made by communities in Kenya. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #12 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — They do not change when you turn around
   Left and right change with the way you face, but north, east, south and west stay the same.

2. B — A sailor
   Sailors use compasses to find direction at sea.

3. D — The meaning of the colours and symbols
   The key tells what each line, colour and symbol stands for.

4. D — Wards
   Sub-counties are divided into wards.

5. D — Low land between hills or mountains
   A valley is a low area between higher land.

6. B — Kenya lies on the equator so temperatures change little
   Near the equator the temperature stays fairly steady, so rain and altitude decide our seasons.

7. D — People needing and helping each other
   Interdependence means we depend on each other.

8. C — Church, mosque or temple
   Places of worship are for prayer.

9. B — 7,000
   7 x 1,000 = 7,000.

10. B — Clustered
   Clustered means close together in a group.

11. B — They can be moved when the family moves
   Portable houses suit families who move with their animals.

12. B — A basket
   The kiondo is a woven basket.

13. C — Honesty
   Honesty is a positive value.

14. D — Say something you like and something to improve, politely
   Kind, helpful feedback improves work.

15. D — Beating pupils
   Teachers are not allowed to beat pupils.

16. A — Maasai Mara
   The Maasai Mara is in Narok County.

17. A — Kericho
   Kericho is a major tea growing area.

18. A — Taking minerals from the ground
   Mining takes minerals such as soda ash or titanium from the earth.

19. C — Treat waste before releasing it
   Treating waste avoids pollution.

20. A — Good roads and nearby workers
   Transport and workers matter.

21. D — Money spent on the project
   Costs are expenses.

22. A — The treasurer
   The treasurer handles and records money.

23. A — Tell a trusted adult
   A trusted adult can help.

24. B — Asking an adult before going online
   Asking permission keeps you safe.

25. B — A quiet place to calm down or talk through a problem
   A peace corner helps pupils settle problems.

26. C — Fear and lost education
   Abuse harms the child's life.

27. C — Cheating
   Buying votes is unfair.

28. C — A teacher patron
   A teacher adviser guides the pupils.

29. D — From the national government and local fees and taxes
   Counties get shared money and collect local fees.

30. B — The Governor
   The governor leads the county.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Profit is the money left after all costs are paid. Profit = income - costs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for formula, 1 mark for correct example.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: 1,100 workers.
   Working / marking points: 700 + 400 = 1,100. 1 mark for adding, 1 mark for correct sum, 1 mark for the unit.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: Plant trees, save water, and reduce waste by reusing and recycling.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: A motto is a short sentence that shows what a school stands for or hopes to achieve.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for short sentence, 1 mark for showing what the school stands for.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: The farmer grows crops and sells them to the trader. The trader carries the crops to town and sells them. The trader needs the crops and the farmer needs the buyer.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: A physical feature is natural, such as a mountain. A built feature is made by people, such as a bridge.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for each correct example.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: County A is larger by 6 squares.
   Working / marking points: 15 - 9 = 6. 1 mark for choosing A, 1 mark for subtracting, 1 mark for 6 squares.

38. (4 marks)
   Answer: A ceremony marks a special event in life, such as a wedding. A festival is a big celebration with many people, such as the Lamu Cultural Festival.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for each example.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: Do not litter, do not write on walls, do not climb or touch old structures, and listen to the guide.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct rule.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Accept the result peacefully, congratulate the winner and offer to help. This keeps peace and shows respect for democracy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

41. (2 marks)
   Answer: The headteacher or teachers, and the school records or log book. Accept old photographs or elders.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each source.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Crops grow, grass grows for animals, and rivers and tanks fill with water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: Say thank you and treat their work with respect. Accept helping them in return.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Dressing, food, housing, artefacts, sports and games, and festivals and ceremonies.
   Working / marking points: 3 marks for all six, 2 marks for four or five, 1 mark for two or three.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Use bright cloth, cut it in a vest shape with a head opening, fix reflective strips across the front and back, and test that it is easy to wear and seen from far.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: How people lived long ago and which tools they used. Accept learning about animals, plants and cultures.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct point.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: A kiondo basket and a soapstone carving. Accept clay pots, beaded jewellery or wooden stools.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each artefact.
